candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Glasgow Coma Scale interpretation
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret a fully testable GCS total of 15 as the maximum possible composite score, while remembering that component responses should also be documented.

options.A: This is the highest possible GCS total when all three components are testable, reflecting the best eye, verbal, and motor responses.
options.B: This is the lowest possible total GCS score, reflecting absent eye, verbal, and motor responses.
options.C: This score is outside the valid GCS range because the scale permits only total scores from 3 through 14.
options.D: This score by itself indicates severe traumatic brain injury and independently requires endotracheal intubation.

candidate.rationale: The official Glasgow Coma Scale resource states that the composite score ranges from 3 to 15, with 3 the lowest possible score and 15 the highest. With all three components testable, 15 represents the maximum total. B and C misstate the scoring range, and D incorrectly interprets a maximum score as severe traumatic brain injury or a standalone airway indication.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The composite GCS score is the sum of eye, verbal, and motor response scores; its possible range is 3–15, with 15 the highest possible total.
